question: Can I add my new spouse or baby to the policy and still get some benefits right away?
expected_answer: Yes, you can get continuity benefit for waiting periods already served, including the first 30 days, specific illness, and pre-existing disease waiting periods.
answer: Yes, you can add your new spouse or baby to the policy within 120 days of marriage or birth [p.12]. However, the Pre-existing Disease clause, exclusions, loading (if any), and Waiting Periods will be applicable to the new spouse or baby, considering the current Policy Year as the first year of the Policy for them [p.24]. But, if you have already served some Waiting Periods, you can provide continuity benefit to your new spouse or baby for those Waiting Periods [p.12].

answer: An act of terrorism means an act or series of acts, including but not limited to the use of force or violence and/or the threat thereof, of any person or group(s) of persons, whether acting alone or on behalf of or in connection with any organization(s) or government(s), or unlawful associations, recognized under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, committed for political, religious, ideological or similar purposes including the intention to influence any government and/or to put the public or any section of the public in fear for such purposes [p.3], [p.4].

expected_answer: I will have two options: convert the policy into a paid-up policy or surrender the policy and receive the Fund Value, after which the policy will terminate.
answer: If the overdue premiums are not paid before the end of the two year revival period, then you will have the following two options: Convert the policy into a paid-up policy or Surrender the policy and receive the Fund Value, at the end of the revival period [p.2].

question: What kind of documents do I need to give to the insurance company if my family member dies in an accident?
expected_answer: Copy of First Investigation Report (FIR), post mortem, panchnama, final police investigation report etc.
answer: You need to provide a Death Certificate, Post-mortem report, and First Investigation Report (FIR), among other documents [p.6]. Additionally, you may need to provide a Copy of all medical tests/ records, admission records, discharge summary, prescriptions etc [p.6]. If you have Personal Accident cover, you need to submit a Death Certificate and Post-mortem report (wherever necessary) [p.9]. You also need to provide Identity proof of Nominee or Original Succession Certificate/Original Legal Heir Certificate or any other proof to the satisfaction of the Company [p.26].
